name: How do you design an ADU for a narrow side yard?

mainEntity.name: How do you design an ADU for a narrow side yard in Burbank or North Hollywood?
mainEntity.text: How do you design an ADU for a narrow side yard in Burbank or North Hollywood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Side-yard ADUs can work well on urban lots, but they need a very efficient design. Narrow sites often favor linear floor plans with open living areas, compact kitchens, stacked plumbing walls, and minimal hallway circulation. The designer must also check whether the unit can maintain required separation from the main house, property lines, and access paths while still allowing light and ventilation. On tight lots, every inch matters, so door swings, appliance sizes, and window placement should be planned early. A side-yard ADU may also benefit from a shed roof or simple gable to reduce structural complexity and keep costs under control. Homeowners should be cautious about designs that look good on paper but leave no room for maintenance access, trash storage, or outdoor use. A narrow-site design works best when it is tailored to the exact dimensions of the property rather than adapted from a generic template.
acceptedAnswer.description: A narrow side-yard ADU usually needs a long, efficient footprint, careful circulation, and a placement that preserves code-required access and separation. The design should avoid wasted hallway space and should account for windows, roof overhangs, and utility clearances.
